visualAction: Establish the recognizable shared meal with particular people and tactile objects; a small allocation interface belongs to the household possibility, not a stock exchange.
The colour and warmth of the Sunday begin thinning; Sera reaches toward her mother’s hand while the plate remains supported on the table. Do not make the mother die or a body disappear.

A separate not-yet-real cradle possibility gains definition while the Sunday’s support decreases. The conflict is between compatible possibilities, not between a real child and a family member’s life.
Sera arrests the withdrawal partway, leaving both possibilities provisional. Do not show the ending’s final loss, a completed sacrifice or a resolved choice.
Several faint differently positioned versions of Sera remain bound to the same household situation, translating compatible histories without literalizing 7D as multiple rooms.
Hold the table’s sensory details and the unresolved resource allocation; the book’s cosmology begins as a personal cost readers can understand.

scenes.alt: A concrete Sunday held as a spatial translation of a 7D silar: Sera at a dining table, her mother’s hand on her shoulder, Taal lingering near a plate of cut fruit. Beside it, a faint empty cradle represents only an uncreated future-child possibility. No room walls, literal building or real infant: the source says a silar is a compatible arrangement of histories and the child has not been born. The7D household is a spatial translation, its withdrawal remains provisional, no infant is born, and later case outcomes stay protected.

visualAction: Faint peripheral versions of Sera become inaccessible as one bodily projection settles onto a surface. They are dimmed beyond access, not killed; do not reveal which later branches are lost.
Sera steadies her breathing with a supported hand and tense shoulders; Kesh adjusts the regulator and waits rather than making a lecture gesture.
Kesh turns the family photograph toward Sera. He is a resident of the world her office may close, with partners and a daughter, not neutral infrastructure.
A descent band marks freedoms unavailable below; the scene contrasts what her body can do with the institutional permission carried by her marn.
Sera tries to orient toward an alternative and returns to the same supported body. Keep the later descent’s rescue, archive encounter, injuries, closed route and time-loop details protected.
Hold Kesh’s particular family beside Sera’s narrowing embodied perspective, explaining why the dimensional vocabulary matters before generalizing it.

visualAction: A higher-level case record arrives at the edge of the composition, then focus moves into the local clerk’s actual task. Use a visual translation of the distant case, not a literal surveillance window falsely representing the velar.
Mira pauses before an instruction to remove named responsibility; her pen does not automatically follow the approved wording.
A restrained portrait detail identifies a mother behind the report. No graphic injury, reenactment of abuse or later rescue outcome is shown.

The official wording replaces identified agents with an impersonal category; Mira keeps the names in a notebook partly under her sleeve. This is source-grounded early method, not an invented new incident.
The report and private note remain physically distinct on the desk while a provisional auditor’s reading position enters the frame; avoid representing the higher observer as morally omniscient.
Hold both records together. The book’s case-file form asks whose account enters the calculation and what disappears when an institution rewrites it.
